findings.finding: The log holds 15,214 events across 1,050 cases and 16 distinct activities.
findings.allowed_wording: The log holds 15,214 events across 1,050 cases and 16 distinct activities.
findings.caveat: Descriptive only - says nothing about whether the process is good.

findings.finding: 295 of 1,050 cases re-enter the process after ending it, producing 296 additional episodes, so the log contains 1,346 episodes of care in total.
findings.caveat: Time between episodes is time OUTSIDE the process and is excluded from every waiting figure below.

findings.finding: 26 departments perform only 8 distinct jobs, judged by which activities each one actually carries out.
findings.allowed_wording: the 26 departments reduce to 8 functional roles
findings.caveat: Roles are grouped by behaviour, not by name. Two departments with the same signature may still be organisationally separate.

findings.finding: The single largest absorber of time is 'CRP  ->  Leucocytes': 746.9 days in total across 1,445 occurrences (12.3% of all measured waiting), median 0 min.
findings.allowed_wording: 'CRP  ->  Leucocytes' absorbs the most total time (12.3% of measured waiting)
findings.caveat: Ranked by TOTAL time absorbed, not by median. A slow step that happens rarely is a smaller problem than a quick one that happens constantly.

findings.finding: The step most out of proportion to how often it happens is 'Admission NC  ->  Release A': it absorbs 7.4x the time its share of transitions would give it (permutation test, p = 0.0025). Classified as handoff because it crosses from one department to another.
findings.allowed_wording: 'Admission NC  ->  Release A' is slow relative to how often it occurs
findings.caveat: This is a DIFFERENT question from the largest absorber of time. A step can dominate the total simply by happening constantly. Says the disproportion is real, not that it is fixable, costly or clinically important.

findings.finding: A further step is also out of proportion: 'CRP  ->  CRP' absorbs 4.53x the time its share of transitions would give it (629.7 days across 317 occurrences, p = 0.0025). Classified as rework because it is a step immediately repeating itself.
findings.allowed_wording: 'CRP  ->  CRP' is also slow relative to how often it occurs
findings.caveat: A SECONDARY bottleneck, held to the same evidence bar as the primary - every step was tested against the same threshold, so this is not a weaker claim. Fixing the largest step will not address this one.

findings.finding: The top 5 of 57 steps account for 53.1% of all measured waiting time. If waiting were spread evenly across steps, 5 of 57 would account for 8.8%.
findings.allowed_wording: the top 5 steps hold 53.1% of the waiting (even spread would give 8.8%)
findings.caveat: Compare the two figures before calling this concentration. Concentration is a reason to target those steps first; it is not evidence that they can be shortened.

findings.finding: 6.8% of all steps are immediately repeated, most often 'Leucocytes' (458 times).
findings.caveat: A repeat is not automatically waste - some are clinically or procedurally required. It marks where to look, not a fault.
